title: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches one light-day (about 25.9 billion km) from Earth on Wed 18 Nov 2026 at 10:16 UTC = 3:46 PM IST (NASA Voyager 1 page countdown); signals take 24 hours each way, about 48 hours for a command and reply; launched 5 Sep 1977, the most distant human-made object, still sending science data while NASA switches instruments off to save power; NASA's Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day: after sunset on Tue 17 Nov, flash VGR (Voyager's call sign) in Morse code (V ...-, G --., R .-.; dots under a second, dashes about a second; repeat about a minute), or use NASA's flasher at go.nasa.gov/vgr.
headline: Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day Away Wednesday, 3:46 PM IST

alt_text: NASA/JPL artist's concept of the Voyager spacecraft in deep space: a large white dish antenna on a gold-coloured body, with instrument booms and a long magnetometer boom reaching across a dark blue, star-filled sky. Headline: Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day Away Wednesday, 3:46 PM IST. Further slides: a signal now takes 24 hours each way, so a command and reply take two days; Voyager 1 is 25.9 billion km away and was launched on 5 Sep 1977; and NASA's call on 17 Nov to flash Voyager's call sign, VGR, in Morse code after sunset.
